preview: Vaishnavi Shah shares her Morgan Stanley Summer Internship interview experience for the Application Development track, detailing the online test and two interview rounds.
content:
Vaishnavi Shah
CE 2019-2023
Morgan Stanley Summer Internship
Overview: (3rd September- Online test, 6th September- Interviews)
Eligibility Criteria: 7.5+ CGPA
They provide 2 tracks: Application Development (App dev) and Enterprise Engineering Track (EE)
I had selected App Dev track.
Round 1: Online Test on AMCAT
Section 1: 20 mins – 10 questions:
Aptitude: MCQs based on statistics, probability, distance/speed, time and work, profit/loss. (Did not solve 2/3)
The problems in this round were of easy to moderate difficulty. Finishing it in 20 minutes was a task.
Section 2: 20 mins – 7 questions
Debugging: Questions with syntactical/logical errors had to be solved. (Did not solve 1/2)
E.g.: Code given to print 1’s when length of array is odd or 0’s when length is even, but the code doesn’t work correctly. Could be an incorrect initialization or wrong condition.
The questions were easy and could be easily solved, the time constraint can be an issue though.
Section 3: 60 mins – 3 questions
Coding section:
These were not the exact questions; they had a long description attached to it. But the underlying solutions were these.
1. https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-valid-parentheses/ (passed 7/9 testcases)
2. https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-intervals/ (passed 10/17 testcases)
3. Don’t remember the exact question but it was a DP based question (passed 12/12 testcases)
For most of these questions, using the brute force approach would also be sufficient. And even partially solving the question can give you an advantage.
The questions were from easy to moderate difficulty.

Round 2: Technical (1 hr. Shortlisted 13- EE 25- App dev track)
Interview started with an introduce yourself question followed by tell me about your favourite project. And then she moved on to technical questions.
I was given a few C++ code snippets and was told to identify the error, if any, and a few questions related to polymorphism and inheritance related to the snippets.
Then asked me about what different data structures exist and then asked me about stacks and queues. I was asked to implement a queue using a stack.
I gave a longer approach at first (a little complex with redundant code) and was asked if it could be simplified. Took a few minutes and then was able to come up with a solution that she wanted.
https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/queue-using-stacks/
Then she moved onto questions related to OS:
How much memory is there in the RAM if there is 8-bit register?
Can I access 2GB file from secondary memory if I only have a 1GB RAM available?
What is virtual memory?
(I was not able to answer most of the OS numerical questions but I was able to answer the theoretical ones. I told her that I am not very sure of this topic. And I gave her my guess for a few questions.)
She then went back to my resume and asked me a few questions about my projects. She asked me if I have any questions for her, and I asked about the projects given to the interns? Any prerequisites required? (Always ask questions!!)

Round 3: Pro-Fit (40 mins. Shortlisted 4-EE 12- App dev)
I was asked to talk about the designing of amazon and the kind of entities that would be present and functions that could be used. (I had a similar project so I described a few entities and then told her about my project :p )
- I was asked about the projects on my resume and technologies used and why?
- How was it working in a team? What do you like about working in a team?
- How have you dealt with situations where you have to work on a project but don’t know the tech stack your team is using? Challenges faced in a team?
- What all would you add, if you are provided funding on one of your projects?
- What if the code you’re working has been deployed and you find a bug in it, what will you do then?
- Why Morgan Stanley?
- Talk about the time where you showed leadership qualities or took an initiative.
Again, I was asked if I have any questions, and I asked about whether the intern gets to select a project, and if I could get an example of a project given to an intern. I also asked about the role of an intern and their responsibilities.
In the end around 930 the same night the results came, 11 of us were selected (2 EE, 9 App dev).

Preparation:
https://github.com/yash0530/InterviewPrepResources
- More than half from every bucket on InterviewBit
- Company wise from GFG
- SDE sheet and videos are a good resource which explains all the approach from brute force to optimal solution. SDE sheet
- OOPs from GFG
- OOPs Design from https://crack-oop-system-design.herokuapp.com/
- OS from GateCrashers / Last Minute Notes
- DBMS from Javatpoint / Last Minute Notes
- Aptitude from Indiabix
- GFG COMPANY ARCHIVES MAIN HAI

Tips:
- For online tests, don’t just spend all your time solving a single question. If you get stuck or can pass only a few test cases then go ahead and solve other questions, and then come back if you get time. Partially solving a question can also increase your chances at being shortlisted.
- Stay hydrated and be confident during an interview.
- Speak out loud while solving a problem, explain your approach.
- Don’t lie on your resume. And revise and prepare a short description about everything that’s there on your resume.
- Prepare for basic HR questions, you can find these by looking at past experiences here or on GFG.
- If you don’t know a certain topic or you are not very sure about it, just tell them.
- Don’t overdo it at the last minute, it can be counterproductive. Just relax and be confident.

ALL THE BEST :)
